findings.title: Documented 'byte-identical rebuild' is false: ffmpeg's native vorbis encoder is non-deterministic run-to-run, and the vault input WAV is never sha256-hashed
findings.evidence: README: 'the transform is deterministic — re-builds the committed OGG byte-identically (the script prints a sha256)'. Re-run this round: script printed sha256 1d981c00... vs committed 7fdb3092...; three identical control encodes of the same PCM -> 2c896ab6..., 5def01b0..., 029724ad... (same 913706 bytes each). Script's only hashlib call hashes OUT_OGG; SRC is never hashed.
findings.detail: Guard bar (d) conjunct 'transform reproducible + sha256-pinned' fails: the PCM stage IS deterministic (0.0482 wrap residual reproduced exactly) but the OGG bytes are not reproducible even on the authoring machine, and no input hash exists to pin provenance.
findings.recommended_fix: Hash+print the vault input sha256 beside the output; make the encode deterministic (a pinned ffmpeg build/container or a deterministic encoder path) and re-pin, OR reword README/PR body to 'PCM stage deterministic; committed artifact sha256-pinned; rebuild verified by decode-compare (duration + decoded-PCM hash), not byte-identity'.

findings.title: Duck-trigger wiring has no test: pending_any_plays and its flush call-site ordering are unpinned
findings.detail: Moving the trigger after a.pending = {} or dropping a family from the OR-list kills ducking silently — all 17 tests stay green. The predicate is pure and headless-testable.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a unit test driving pending_any_plays over each family (each >0 -> true; zeroed Pending -> false) in audio_test.odin.

findings.title: The '0.4+ amplitude' hard-cut click figure does not reproduce — actual hard-cut wrap jump at the documented window is 0.127 peak
findings.evidence: README: 'A hard cut would click (0.4+ amplitude — the track has no beat-lockable phrase boundary)'. Recomputed from the vault WAV with the script's own math: |seg[L-1]-seg[0]| pre-crossfade at [41.4s,167.0s] = 0.1267 peak (also the max 1-sample jump in the window). The 0.048 residual claim reproduces exactly (0.0482).
findings.detail: README, PR body, and spec-ambience-bed.md:179 all carry the 0.4+ figure; it is >3x overstated. The design conclusion (crossfade needed) still holds — 0.127 >> 0.048 — but the documented number is wrong.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace '0.4+ amplitude' with the measured ~0.13 one-sample wrap jump in README.md, _pr_body_ambience.md, and spec-ambience-bed.md.

findings.title: test_bed_duck_never_raises cannot fail at the shipped constants — cap removal goes undetected
findings.evidence: MUSIC_VOLUME :: f32(0.40); MUSIC_DUCK_VOLUME :: f32(0.12); duck_ratio := min(MUSIC_DUCK_VOLUME / MUSIC_VOLUME, 1.0) — at these constants the uncapped ratio is 0.3, so 'multiplier <= 1.0' and 'ducked level <= master' pass with or without the min cap.
findings.detail: Deleting the cap keeps every test green until MUSIC_VOLUME is retuned at/below MUSIC_DUCK_VOLUME. The guard the test names is not load-bearing.
findings.recommended_fix: Parameterize bed_duck_multiplier/bed_level over master and duck volumes (pure inputs) so a test can drive the master-below-duck case directly.

findings.title: pending_any_plays doc comment overpromises: the flush's play loops do not key off it, so a fifth family CAN still silently miss the duck
findings.evidence: 'The duck trigger and (implicitly) the flush's play loops both key off it.' — but the flush enumerates families separately (audio.odin:374-389); the helper is called only by the duck trigger.
findings.detail: A future fifth play family requires editing both the play loops and this helper — exactly the lockstep hazard the comment claims is eliminated. Code is correct today; the comment misstates the invariant.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword the comment, or derive both the play loops and the helper from one shared family table.
